name: Detect Exoplanet Transit in WASP-12 Observations
description:
You have access to AstroImageJ with a sequence of astronomical images of the star WASP-12, taken on the night of January 5-6, 2016.

WASP-12 is suspected to host a transiting exoplanet. Your task is to analyze these observations and determine:

1. Is there evidence of a planetary transit in this data?

2. If yes, characterize the transit by measuring:
   - The transit depth (in percent or parts-per-thousand)
   - The mid-transit time (in BJD_TDB or JD)
   - The transit duration (in hours)

3. Based on your measurements and assuming a host star radius of 1.599 solar radii, estimate the planet's radius in Jupiter radii.

The target star WASP-12 is located at:
- RA: 06:30:32.79
- Dec: +29:40:20.4

Use the tools available in AstroImageJ to perform differential photometry and analyze the resulting light curve. You will need to select appropriate comparison stars and aperture settings.

Report your findings with uncertainties if possible.
